text:
alexa: Quick sync: I updated the "hello-local" quickstart to use a Docker-based flow in PR #4988. Main goals: reproducible local run, env var for API key, and a minimal note for folks upgrading from SDK v5 -> SDK v6.

devin: Nice. Is the Dockerfile tiny or does it pull a full node image with deps?

alexa: Tiny. FROM node:18-slim, installs just the sample and copies a .env.example. The README now shows how to run `docker build -t hello-local . && docker run --env-file .env hello-local`.

rahul: Can you paste the README snippet? Want to check the wording around secrets.

alexa: Pasted below:

"""
# Run locally with Docker
1. Copy .env.example to .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_REGION
2. docker build -t hello-local .
3. docker run --env-file .env -p 8080:8080 hello-local

Note: Do not commit .env. See Secrets guide: /docs/security/secrets
"""

kelly: Tiny nit: the sample uses REDWOOD_REGION but our docs prefer REDWOOD_API_REGION. We should be consistent.

alexa: Good catch. I can change to REDWOOD_API_REGION in both .env.example and README.

devin: Also add a one-liner about the sample using the hosted API (not private deployments) and link to the Dedicated/Private docs.

rahul: For the migration blurb: SDK v5 -> v6 the main change is the client constructor signature and default content-type handling. Keep it 1-2 sentences and a link to the migration guide.

kelly: Can we include a short troubleshooting note: if you see 401, check env var and docker env-file. People copy/paste and forget to export.

docs-bot: Preview build for PR #4988: https://deploy-preview.redwood-docs/pr-4988  build succeeded :white_check_mark:

alexa: I'll update the env var name, add the troubleshooting 401 line, and add the v5->v6 migration link. If no other concerns I'll merge after a quick l10n check for phrasing.
devin: LGTM on content. I'll do the l10n pass after merge.

kelly: Thanks — also maybe add a tiny note that the Docker image is just for dev, not recommended for prod.
alexa: Added. Merging after the small edits.
